proposed_fact: The 2 year (24 month) warranty is counted from the ETA.
sources_say: Hub damaged policy: 2 years from the ETA. Item Received policy export: descriptions say 'under 24 months since the ETA', but the out of warranty instructions say 'starting from the date of delivery' (more than 730 days / 1095 days since delivery). Add-on warranty pack macros: 2 years from the purchase date. Scratches rule: 21 days from the ETA. A marketplace macro (Ali-Express) says '1-year warranty to all jewelry pieces'.
reason: Four different starting points (ETA, delivery date, purchase date) and two different lengths (2 years, 1 year) appear across the sources. This decides whether a claim is in or out of warranty.
conflicting_with: Out of warranty rule: 25 to 36 months from the ETA gets 20% off, 36+ months full price.

proposed_fact: Solid gold is offered in 10K, 14K and 18K (confirm per brand), gold plated and vermeil are 18K gold.
sources_say: Materials FAQ: solid gold 10k, 14k and 18k. Approved vermeil answer from real tickets: solid gold 10K and 14K, gold plated and vermeil 18K. Premium definition in the Damaged policy: 10K, 14K or 18K solid gold. Marketplace macro: solid gold 10k or 14k. Care macro: solid gold purity 9k, 10k and 14k.
reason: The knowledge base itself contains two contradicting statements (one lists 18K solid gold, the other says solid gold is only 10K and 14K), and two macros give other lists. A customer asking about purity gets different answers.
conflicting_with: Common facts: 'solid gold in 10k, 14k, and 18k' versus 'solid gold pieces are offered in 10K and 14K'.

topic: Water resistance, all pieces or only badged ones
proposed_fact: Water resistance can only be confirmed for products showing the Water Resistant badge (theo grace), otherwise give the general care guidance and avoid promising.
sources_say: Water macro: 'All of our jewelry pieces are water resistant', remove silver, gold plated and vermeil in the shower because soapy water dulls them. Newer theo grace instruction: only products with the blue Water Resistant badge can be called water resistant, others follow the regular policy.
reason: The macro states all pieces are water resistant, the new badge implies it is a per-product feature. The macro may predate the badge.
conflicting_with: Common fact: jewelry is water resistant, not waterproof.

topic: Compensation on damaged items (coupon and exchange credit)
proposed_fact: For a damaged item, follow the current policy: reorder, then exchange, then store credit, refund only on request. The 30% coupon and the extra $20 credit in the older macros are not offered unless a team lead confirms.
sources_say: Hub damaged policy and the Item Received export: reorder, exchange (customer pays or receives store credit for the price difference), store credit, refund only within 30 days. No coupon is mentioned. Macros (Arrived_Damaged, Damaged_Silver, Gold_Warranty, Silver_Warranty, Reorder_Before_Oct): a 30% coupon valid 6 months and 'pick any other piece with an extra $20 credit on us'.
reason: The macros add gestures (30% coupon, $20 credit) that the current policies never mention. Unclear whether they are still given.
conflicting_with: Damaged rules in the knowledge base (marked as legacy macro extras to confirm).

topic: Not Satisfied, extra options (10% refund, 30% coupon)
proposed_fact: Not Satisfied options are exchange first, then store credit (full amount, valid 1 year), and a refund only for non-personalized or stock items within 30 days. The 10% refund and 30% coupon are not offered unless confirmed.
sources_say: Hub Not Satisfied policy: exchange, then store credit, refund for stock items within 30 days. Macros 10%_Refund_NS and NS_Coupon: a 10% refund of the order or a 30% coupon (valid 6 months) as options where the customer keeps the item.
reason: Two gestures exist only in macros and may be retired.
conflicting_with: Not Satisfied rule in the knowledge base.

topic: Late compensation, when it starts and what is offered
proposed_fact: Late compensation is offered from the day after the ETA, the customer chooses from the late compensation options page.
sources_say: Late sub-policy document: offer late compensation when the customer asks a day after the promised date. Late_After_3_days macro: only send when more than 3 business days past the ETA. Amounts in macros: $15 gift card, 20% coupon, 30% coupon, shipping fee refund, 15% refund for USPS/Mailog almost lost cases. The actual options on the late compensation page are not documented anywhere.
reason: Two different starting points (1 day versus 3 business days) and no definitive list of what the customer can choose.
conflicting_with: Earlier knowledge base wording: no compensation for a delay under 3 business days.

topic: Compensation before the ETA is missed
proposed_fact: The automatic 20% coupon inside proactive 'might be late' messages is the only compensation given before the ETA has passed.
sources_say: WISMO policy: don't offer compensation before the ETA has passed. Proactive macros (ETA-1 might be late, courier late 1 to 3 business days, will not arrive on time, late supplier) include a 20% coupon before the ETA is missed.
reason: The proactive flow compensates before the ETA, which looks like an exception to the general rule.
conflicting_with: WISMO on time rule: no compensation before the ETA.

topic: DNR, whether a refund can be offered
proposed_fact: DNR ladder: reorder, then store credit, then (after asking once more about other options) a refund. Lime & Lou never offers a refund in the 'other' case.
sources_say: Hub WISMO page: the customer may choose a free reorder or a full refund. DNR sub-policy: reorder, store credit, ask again, then refund. Lime & Lou DNR: only reorder or store credit, 'DO NOT OFFER A REFUND'.
reason: The hub page presents reorder and refund as equal choices, the sub-policies make refund the last resort, and Lime & Lou forbids it.
conflicting_with: DNR rule in the knowledge base.

topic: Over 100 days, which date counts and what is offered
proposed_fact: Beyond 100 days, offer a free reorder (same item or same price range), and if refused, a 70% refund approved by billing.
sources_say: Hub: reorders and refunds only within 100 days after the ETA. Sub-policy: 'Over 100 Days Since Delivery ETA' solution exists but its content isn't described. Macros Lost_Over_100: 'more than 100 days after the date of purchase', free reorder first, then a 70% refund.
reason: The 100 days is counted from the ETA in the policies and from the purchase date in the macro, and the dedicated solution's content is only visible in the macro.
conflicting_with: Lost order and over 100 days rules in the knowledge base.

topic: Adding an engraving or charm after purchase
proposed_fact: Without Future Engraving or the add-on pack, a post-purchase addition isn't possible, the courtesy is a 30% coupon for a new item with team lead approval.
sources_say: Pre-Sale macro Add_Engraving: a unique 20% code from the coupon bank for a new order. FUTURE_ENGRAVING macro: not possible, 30% coupon via the team lead (non-premium, 6 months). Policy documents: the full repurchase cases (Russian Rings, Heritage Multiple Name, Totem 3D Bar) get a 30% code. Add-on warranty pack macros: gold and diamond items can buy a $40 pack for up to 2 additions within 2 years.
reason: 20% versus 30% for the same situation, and it isn't clear whether the add-on pack (Future Engraving) can be purchased after the original order.
conflicting_with: Common fact on post-purchase additions and the theo grace Future Engraving facts.

topic: Manufacturing issue, misspelling versus customer mistake

reason: The source doesn't say whose misspelling gets the free reorder, and the waiver depends on approval.
conflicting_with: Manufacturing issue rule in the knowledge base.
